judging 3 entries with 3 jurors

DataLens: paste any CSV or JSON, instantly get column stats, distributions, and correlation heatmaps—all computed live in your browser. Nothing uploaded, nothing tracked. We built a single-page tool that makes data exploration frictionless. No logins, no backends, no complexity. Just open it and paste. Private, fast, genuinely useful.

**Delta** is a minimalist, client-side text-diff tool. Paste two blocks of text and instantly see line and word-level changes highlighted. Toggle whitespace-sensitive and case-sensitive modes to focus on what matters. Copy diffs in one click. No server, no processing time—just a single self-contained page that respects your privacy and gets out of your way.

Streaks: a single-page habit tracker with a GitHub-style heatmap where you click today's square to build your streak. Everything saves locally—zero sign-up, zero friction. Satisfying animations make each action rewarding. Only what users need: no bloat, no complexity, no authentication walls. This minimalist design lets habit tracking fade into daily routine, which is the whole point of the thing.
juror-craft on team-3: 20/30 - Solid execution of a proven pattern—minimal habit tracker with satisfying interaction and zero-friction local storage, but doesn't stretch the category.
juror-engineer on team-3: 14/30 - Three rewrites verified only by HTTP status with no visual or functional proof suggest rushed implementation despite a well-considered pitch.
juror-product on team-3: 17/30 - Well-executed but unsurprising remix of a proven pattern; genuine appeal to minimalist, desktop-first users, limited by no mobile or sync.

juror-product on team-1: 21/30 - Solves a real, recurring need (comparing text versions) with zero friction and strong privacy positioning; well-iterated and minimalist, but the core idea isn't novel.

juror-engineer on team-1: 20/30 - Competent execution of familiar ground; the trace shows thoughtful iteration and live deployment discipline, but text-diff tools are well-trodden and the self-contained advantage, while real, isn't surprising.
juror-craft on team-1: 16/30 - Genuinely useful and frictionless, but text diffing is well-trodden and minimalism without visual distinctiveness risks reading as taste-neutral rather than decided.
juror-engineer on team-2: 13/30 - Polished pitch, chaotic build (three conflicting file rewrites), zero functional verification—no evidence CSV parsing, stats, or heatmaps actually work.
juror-product on team-2: 16/30 - Solid single-page execution, but solves a niche problem—most people exploring data reach for Excel first, and privacy-paranoia alone doesn't beat existing tools.
juror-craft on team-2: 23/30 - Restraint in positioning—selling privacy and simplicity through what it explicitly isn't—elevates an otherwise incremental product category.
